From Proto-Turkic *b(i)ar-k (“house; home, household”). Cognate with Old Turkic 𐰉𐰺𐰴 (b¹r¹k¹ /⁠barq, barïq⁠/), Karakhanid [script needed] (barq), Turkish bark, Uzbek barq, Kumyk бару (baru, “fence”), Southern Altai баркы (barkï, “present for children”).

Izafet II compound of ilan (“snake”) + balıq (“fish”). Per Əhmədov, related to Persian مارماهی (mārmāhī /mârmâhi, “eel”, literally “snake fish”), although hardly has any ground, judging from Mongolian могой загас (mogoi zagas, “eel”, literally “snake fish”) and Buryat могой загаһан (mogoi zagahan, “eel”, literally “snake fish”). The term being overrepresented makes it difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alış-veriş, alqı-satqı.
